## Source inspected
The November/December 1995 *Guardian* PDF was downloaded from HEU’s public archive on 20 September 2026. It is a 16-page image scan (no text layer). Cover and the CSIL passage on page 9 were read from rendered page images. OCR was used as a finding aid; wording below was checked against the page image.
:::

## Annotation

The cover feature is about agency/home nursing for an 89-year-old Vancouver man with Alzheimer’s, not a CSIL how-to. On page 9 the article explains how the family obtained Ministry of Health money after other revenues ran out:

> a new program of the Community Support Branch of the Continuing Care Division called “Choice in Supports for Independent Living” or CSIL. Designed as a pilot program for people with disabilities who want to take more responsibility for managing their own care, the scheme allows non-profit societies to receive direct funding to hire caregivers for community-based care.

Further statements on that page, as read from the scan:

- Sally Hamilton “manages the program for the ministry.”
- Of “65,000 continuing care clients in the province, only 130 access CSIL funds,” and “only one other is an Alzheimer patient.”
- The family formed a society and secured “$3,540 a month.”
- Hamilton is quoted that the ministry expects CSIL employers “to pay within the unionized range, provide statutory benefits and keep a small cushion in the event of emergency.”

This is contemporaneous 1995 public description of CSIL as a **new / pilot** Ministry of Health program housed in **Community Support Branch / Continuing Care Division**. That independently attests the administrative home named in the commissioning issue. It does **not** date the pilot’s start to 1993, 1994, or 1995, and it does not name ECPM, Gauthier, or Creekview.

`source_type` is `primary`. HEU is a union newspaper with an interest in unionized home-support wages; treat cost and “pilot” wording as HEU’s contemporaneous report, not as a ministry instrument.

## Limitations

- Image scan; some numerals and small type are easy to misread. The 130 / 65,000 / $3,540 figures should be re-checked on a printed copy before they are used as statistics.
- The Henderson case is an Alzheimer’s family-society use of CSIL, presented as exceptional.
- “Designed as a pilot” in late 1995 can mean still piloting, recently piloted, or loosely “new.” It does not by itself settle province-wide 1995.

## Open questions

- Hamilton’s exact title and the instrument that created Community Support Branch CSIL.
- Whether 130 clients is a province-wide pilot census or a snapshot of approved cases.
- How this “non-profit societies” description relates to later CSIL Phase I (individual employer) / Phase II (client support group) language.
